    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.
Både Timon Haugan og Henrik Kristoffersen tapte halvannet sekund til Braathen i første omgang. Begge fortsatte å skuffe i andre omgang og ble henholdsvis 18 og 19.
– Jeg kjørte i en stein, forteller Kristoffersen til TV 2.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/flystansen-i-usa_-bytting-av-kabel-mulig-arsak-1.18082036</link>
      <description>USAs transportminister Sean Duffy sier utskiftning av en kobbertråd kan være årsaken til den omfattende flystansen fredag.
Flere enn 15.000 flygninger ble forsinket eller innstilt da amerikanske luftfartsmyndigheter FAA i fire timer nektet alle fly å ta av på grunn av forstyrrelser i flykontrollen.
På en pressekonferanse lørdag sa transportminister Duffy at problemene kan ha oppstått som følge av arbeidet med å bytte ut gamle kobberkabler med fiber ved et av FAAs anlegg.
Ministeren oppgav også navnet på selskapet han mente hadde forsårsaket problemene. Hendelsen skal granskes videre.
Det er fremdeles etterslep etter fredagens problemer. Lørdag er flere enn 10.000 flygninger innstilt eller forsinket, ifølge FlightAware.</description>

      <title>Kraftig brann i Lillestrøm</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/stor-oslo/kraftig-brann-i-lillestrom-1.18081998</link>
      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen, og de vil etterforske saken videre.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Solbakken overrasker – Aasgaard inn i startelleveren</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

      <description>En eldre kvinnelig bilfører kjørte ned tre personer i Lyngdal.

      <description>Britisk politi bekrefter overfor BBC at de har innledet en etterforskning mot komikeren David Walliams for alvorlige seksuelle forbrytelser.
Det skjer etter at flere kvinner har stått frem med anklager om at Walliams skal ha brukt kjendisstatusen sin for å tilnærme seg unge kvinner seksuelt.

Han har avvist å ha gjort noe galt.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Thore «Henki» Holm Hansen er død</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/thore-_henki_-holm-hansen-er-dod-1.18081252</link>
      <description>Den tidligere Outlaws-sjefen og countrymusikeren er død, 82 år gammel, melder VG.
Holm Hansen ledet MC-klubben Outlaws, ble dømt for handel med narkotika og våpen og ga ut countrymusikk.
«Han sovnet stille inn på morgenen i dag, hjemme hos meg i sin egen seng, med venner og familie rundt seg», skriver datteren hans June Nordlie i et innlegg på Facebook.
Holm Hansen ble i 1981 dømt til 60 års fengsel i en kokainsak i USA, men ble besluttet deportert til Norge.
Selv hevdet han at dommen var et justismord, og knyttet saken til påstått arbeid for CIA.</description>

      <description>Microsoft opplever tekniske problemer som rammer brukere av blant annet e-posttjenesten Outlook og Teams. Selskapet opplyser at de jobber med å løse saken.

      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.

      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Komiker David Walliams anklaget for grooming</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/komiker-david-walliams-anklaget-for-grooming-1.18078634</link>
      <description>Den britiske komikeren og skuespilleren David Walliams anklages av ei rekke kvinner for å ha brukt kjendisstatusen sin for å tilnærme seg unge kvinner seksuelt.
Det skriver The Guardian og ITV News, som sammen har jobbet med saken.
Minst to kvinner framholder at de var mindreårige da Walliams først tok kontakt med dem.
Walliams nekter for anklagene.
Walliams prøvde å gå rettens vei for å stoppe de britiske avisene fra å navngi ham i saken, men fikk ikke medhold.
Han er blant annet kjent fra TV-serien «Little Britain» og som dommer for underholdningsprogrammet «Britain's Got Talent».</description>

]]> 1361478 Lawyers unsure if extra funding can reduce massive caseload at Federal Court https://cheknews.ca/lawyers-unsure-if-extra-funding-can-reduce-massive-caseload-at-federal-court-1361485/ Sun, 15 Nov 2026 19:55:43 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361485

The recent federal budget included $58 million in additional funding court administration but the Federal Court still doesn't have a clear picture of how it can be used to reduce a massive caseload that has grown rapidly since 2020.

The post Lawyers unsure if extra funding can reduce massive caseload at Federal Court appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The recent federal budget included $58 million in additional funding court administration but the Federal Court still doesn’t have a clear picture of how it can be used to reduce a massive caseload that has grown rapidly since 2020.

“At the moment, the Federal Court doesn’t have additional details on how the funding confirmed will be distributed among the stated purposes,” Chief Justice Alan Diner told The Canadian Press in an emailed statement on Thursday.

The Federal Court hears immigration-related issues such as visa applications, refugee claims, admissibility cases and removals. It has responsibility for upholding the law in other areas related to federal jurisdiction, like intellectual property, national security and Indigenous rights.

The court asked for additional resources to handle a caseload that’s ballooned to nearly 31,000 proceedings commenced as of Sept. 30 this year — up from about 7,600 in all of 2020.

More than 27,000 of the proceedings started this year are immigration cases.

Diner told The Canadian Press in an August interview that judges and court staff have had to work evenings, weekends and vacation days to handle a caseload that has been growing in large part because of immigration matters.

The budget says the money is earmarked for the Courts Administration Service, which serves the Federal Court, the Federal Appeal Court, the Tax Court of Canada and the Court Martial Appeal Court of Canada.

The single mention of it in the documents published Nov. 5 says the new funding is meant to address the Federal Court caseload and to help the Courts Administration Service with Official Languages Act compliance, a translation backlog and the need to modernize court infrastructure.

The extra $58 million in funding is set to begin in the 2027/28 fiscal year and continue for four years, averaging $14.5 million annually.

Joannie Fogue, spokesperson for Justice Minister Sean Fraser, said the funding is meant to “strengthen the national courts,” respond to resource challenges and build workload efficiencies. But exactly how it will be allocated aren’t yet known.

“We are continuing to work through the details and implications of the funding commitment and are awaiting further information on the how allocation will be distributed,” she said in a media statement.

While the court awaits more details, immigration lawyers question whether the additional money from Ottawa will do much to move cases through the court more efficiently, given how the demands have grown.

“Any increase in funding is positive, but it’s a modest increase and the increase in the Federal Court’s immigration caseload has been anything but modest,” said Jacqueline Bonisteel, an Ottawa-based immigration lawyer.

While Bonisteel said the additional funding is welcome, she doesn’t see how $58 million spread over four years will be enough, given the spike in the caseload.

“It’s not going to be enough to cope with the issues that the court’s seeing right now, a 600 per cent increase in immigration caseload since 2020,” she said.

“The current compliment of judges and the current resources that the court has just simply aren’t enough to deal with that magnitude of an increase.”

Bonisteel said it can take “upwards of two years” now to get an immigration case through the court.

Zeynab Moayyed, a Toronto-based immigration lawyer, agreed the problems at the Federal Court go beyond what $58 million could fix.

Moayyed cited a shortage of registry staff in the court and said routine paperwork that used to take about a day to process — like a filing for a judicial review — now takes weeks.

Moayyed attributed the increase in caseload in part to more people filing mandamus applications meant to force a decision from the Immigration Department when people are facing long delays.

But both Moayyed and Bonisteel said the quality of Immigration Department decisions has declined since the feds adopted artificial intelligence tools and new software in a bid to review and process applications more quickly.

The lack of human interaction at the department is turning small problems into large ones and pushing them onto the court’s plate, they said.

“Previously, (lawyers) could reach out to (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada), to program managers, to visa office managers and so on. And … if it was a mistake they would receive a reconsideration and that matter would be reopened, and if it wasn’t a mistake, (the applicant) would understand what they did wrong,” Moayyed said.

“But with the coming into effect of those tools, at the same time we had the shutting down of informal ways of addressing areas that happen in the system, and applicants started turning to Federal Court.”

Bonisteel said the department could ease the Federal Court’s workload by finding a way to streamline requests for reconsideration before they get shunted to the court.

“These are very multi-faceted problems and they need multi-faceted solutions. So it’s not just about court funding. It’s about addressing the systemic issues that are leading to the increase in the court’s caseload,” she said.

The Immigration Department has said it uses AI and advanced analytics tools under human oversight at all times. The department says these AI tools do not make decisions and are meant to assist with tasks like triaging applications, identifying routine cases, generating case summaries and answering client questions through chatbots.

The department’s first AI strategy, released earlier this year, says the goal is to get the technology to reduce application backlogs and wait times.

Moayyed said those long delays are causing “a great deal of distress” for people stuck in the system.

“Our job, in addition to being immigration lawyers, has become confidant and the therapist for a client, listening to them talk about having their life on hold and in limbo until they get a decision,” she said.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 14, 2026.

The post Lawyers unsure if extra funding can reduce massive caseload at Federal Court appeared first on CHEK.

A brand of brown rice distributed in British Columbia and six other provinces is being recalled due to the presence of insects, according to the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA).

In a recall notice issued Nov. 13, the CFIA said Tree of Life Canada is recalling Producers brand Brown Rice sold in 22.6-kilogram packages.

The affected product was distributed to hotels, restaurants and institutions in B.C., Alberta, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario and Quebec.

The agency is advising businesses and institutions not to use, sell, serve or distribute the affected product.

The recall applies to packages with the UPC 0 72806 00225 0 and the following codes:

  • 11/09/26, 13326PRM
  • 11/10/26, 13426PRM
  • 12/12/26, 16626PRM
  • 12/14/26, 16826PRM

The recall, initiated on Nov. 10, has been classified as a Class 3 recall, meaning the product is unlikely to cause adverse health consequences.

The CFIA has not specified which insects were found in the rice or identified which businesses in B.C. received the affected product.

Anyone with questions about the recall can contact the CFIA at 1-613-773-2342 or by email at information@inspection.gc.ca.

]]> 1361457 Wolf warning still in effect at Long Beach, Parks Canada reminds public https://cheknews.ca/wolf-warning-still-in-effect-at-long-beach-parks-canada-reminds-public-1361441/ Sun, 15 Nov 2026 18:53:40 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361441

Parks Canada is reminding visitors to exercise caution in the Long Beach area of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, where a family of five wolves continues to roam and show a heightened interest in dogs.

The post Wolf warning still in effect at Long Beach, Parks Canada reminds public appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Parks Canada is reminding visitors to exercise caution in the Long Beach area of Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, where a family of five wolves continues to roam and show a heightened interest in dogs.

The agency confirmed in a Facebook post Friday that a wolf-in-area warning remains in effect for the entire Long Beach unit, located between Tofino and Ucluelet on Vancouver Island’s west coast.

“Reports of wolf interactions, both with and without dogs present, have continued through the fall, and the wolves continue to show a high interest in dogs,” Parks Canada said in the update.

A prohibition on dogs remains in effect from Green Point Rocks to the southern boundary of the Long Beach Unit, though leashed dogs are still permitted in certain other areas of the national park reserve.

The warning was originally issued on Sept. 18, 2025, following reports of increasingly bold behaviour by wolves, including attempts to prey on dogs.

In February, a wolf attack on a dog prompted an expanded closure of areas in the park, though the dog was not injured.

According to Parks Canada, the wolves have demonstrated an increasing willingness to approach visitors and have attempted to prey on large dogs, including those on leashes.

The agency says the animals are also showing signs of habituation, meaning they are becoming increasingly accustomed to the presence of humans.

The warning remains in effect until further notice.

In the meantime, Parks Canada is encouraging visitors to leave their dogs at home when exploring the Long Beach Unit.

Visitors are also advised to carry bear spray and know how to use it, keep children close, hike in groups and remain alert for signs of wildlife activity, including tracks and droppings.

Despite the warning, Parks Canada emphasizes that wolves are a natural and important part of the coastal ecosystem.

“By giving wildlife space and following park regulations, we can help keep both people and wildlife safe,” the agency said.

Non-compliance with closures, dog bans or leash laws can result in charges under the Canada National Parks Act, with penalties up to $25,000.

Heavy rain and wind has hit much of Vancouver Island over the weekend, triggering new high streamflow advisories, widespread power outages and warnings about dangerous coastal waves, with more rain to come.

Environment Canada has maintained rainfall warnings Sunday for northern, western and inland Vancouver Island, as well as eastern Vancouver Island from Courtenay to Campbell River.

The storm is expected to bring totals of 80 to 150 millimetres of rain to areas around Zeballos, Gold River and Port Alice, while Tofino and communities farther south were expected to see between 50 and 100 millimetres.

Around Courtenay and Campbell River, rainfall totals were expected to reach approximately 50 millimetres.

Much of the heaviest rain has already fallen, with conditions expected to ease through Sunday afternoon and into the evening.

Environment Canada says heavy rainfall will transition to moderate rain across western and northern areas Sunday afternoon before tapering to light showers overnight.

Despite improving conditions, the weather agency warns that pooling water, reduced visibility and washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts remain possible.

Thousands without power, entire village of Zeballos affected

The storm has also caused thousands of power outages across Vancouver Island.

According to BC Hydro, as of 10:30 a.m. Sunday, 23 outages were affecting 2,291 customers on northern Vancouver Island, while another four outages were affecting 550 customers in the south.

That brings the total to more than 2,800 customers affected by outages across the Island.

Among the hardest-hit communities is Zeballos, where the entire village has been left without power.

BC Hydro says specialized equipment must be transported to the repair site by helicopter because of the remote location and challenging terrain.

Crews attempted to reach the site Saturday, but poor weather prevented them from safely carrying out repairs.

Another attempt to reach the site was planned for Sunday, weather permitting.

There is currently no estimated time for power to be restored.

New high streamflow advisory issued for Comox Valley rivers

The BC River Forecast Centre issued a new high streamflow advisory Sunday morning for Dove Creek and the Tsolum River on eastern Vancouver Island.

The advisory follows approximately 30 to 50 millimetres or more of rainfall recorded near Courtenay and Comox between Saturday and Sunday.

River levels rose rapidly overnight, with flows in Dove Creek reaching levels associated with a five- to 10-year return period. The Tsolum River was experiencing flows in the two- to five-year return period range and was continuing to rise.

Another 10 to 20 millimetres of rain could fall in the area Sunday, potentially pushing river levels higher.

The new advisory comes after the River Forecast Centre downgraded flood watches for northern, western and central Vancouver Island to high streamflow advisories on Friday.

Those advisories include the Sproat and Somass rivers near Port Alberni, where cumulative rainfall and slower river responses are expected to keep water levels elevated through the weekend.

A high streamflow advisory means river levels are rising or expected to rise rapidly, although major flooding is not anticipated. Minor flooding in low-lying areas remains possible.

Officials are warning residents to stay away from fast-moving rivers and unstable banks, and never attempt to drive through flooded roads or river crossings.

Extreme wave hazard along Vancouver Island’s west coast

Meanwhile, Parks Canada is warning of dangerous coastal conditions along Vancouver Island’s west coast, with waves expected to reach six to eight metres on Sunday.

An extreme wave hazard advisory remains in effect through Nov. 15 for Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, including beaches and shorelines around Ucluelet and Tofino.

Parks Canada says peak wave activity is expected Sunday afternoon, coinciding with high tides and strong winds.

Large waves could produce powerful currents and flooding along upper shorelines, with some beaches going from dry to several feet underwater in seconds.

Parks Canada warns that surging waves can move large logs and potentially reach beyond beaches into parking areas.

Visitors are urged to avoid entering the water and stay well back from beaches, rocky shorelines and driftwood.

For those hoping to watch the storm, Parks Canada recommends viewing from safer elevated locations, including the Florencia Bay Look-out and the observation deck at the Kwisitis Visitor Centre.

Temporary closures of beaches and parking areas may be implemented if conditions worsen.

The stratospheric polar vortex has been disturbed by the earliest warming on record. But what is the polar vortex, and what happens when it’s disrupted?

The polar vortex is a large area of low pressure and swirling cold air parked over the North and South Poles. When it’s strong, it contains cold air there. It’s like an atmospheric ring trapping cold air in the polar regions.

When the vortex weakens over the North Pole and becomes wavy or splits in half, cold air plunges south. This happens fairly regularly in winter and leads to Arctic air outbreaks.

Polar vortex versus record-breaking El Niño

The fact that it’s been disturbed by the earliest warming on record this year would typically signal frigid temperatures ahead. But we’re also dealing with a record-breaking El Niño and Super El Niño, which usually means a very mild and warmer-than-normal winter for Canada.


Environment and Climate Change Canada’s seasonal forecasts continue to show a very high probability for above-normal temperatures for November, December and into January 2027.

The historic El Niño and Super El Niño could cancel out or temper the potential impact of a disrupted polar vortex this winter.
